memory_annotations.evidence_summary: No durable preference evidence was expressed; all choices were limited to the timing, cost, and logistics of this Chicago conference trip.

messages.content: I need to put together my Chicago trip for the university-press rights conference in late March. The conference runs Thursday through Sunday, and I need both flights from Denver and a hotel near the venue.
I can compare complete flight-and-hotel combinations. What are the exact dates, where is the conference being held, and which Thursday and Sunday events determine your arrival and departure times?

It is March 27 through March 30 at the Palmer House. There is an exhibitor briefing at 6:30 Thursday evening that I cannot miss. The final Sunday session ends at 2:30. I also have an office commitment in Denver Thursday morning and will not be able to leave for the airport before 10:30.

That makes Thursday departures around noon or shortly afterward the workable range. Denver-to-Chicago nonstop flights generally take about two and a half hours, and Chicago is one hour ahead, so I would target an arrival at O'Hare or Midway no later than about 4:30 p.m. That leaves some margin for getting downtown and checking in before 6:30. On Sunday, a flight before about 5:30 p.m. would be risky after a 2:30 finish. Is one traveler going, and should I compare economy fares and standard rooms?
Yes, just me. Economy and a standard room are fine. I need a realistic amount of time to get from the airport to the hotel; I do not want an itinerary that works only if everything goes perfectly.

Understood. I will exclude Thursday arrivals after 4:30 and Sunday departures before 5:30. For planning, Midway usually offers the shorter trip to the Palmer House, while O'Hare has more flight choices but can take longer. Do you have a ceiling for the combined flight and three hotel nights, or should I first show the strongest combinations at different price points?
Show me a few sensible combinations first. I can judge the price once I see what the schedule and hotel tradeoffs look like.

Here are three current combinations to compare, with taxes included where the listing provides them. Option A: Southwest nonstop from Denver at 12:05 p.m., arriving Midway at 3:25 p.m.; return Sunday at 6:35 p.m., arriving Denver at 8:15 p.m. The round trip is about $328. Stay at the Palmer House for three nights at an estimated $864 total. Combined estimate: $1,192. This is the simplest conference setup and gives you about three hours from landing to the briefing. Option B: United nonstop at 12:20 p.m., arriving O'Hare at 3:45 p.m.; return at 6:10 p.m., arriving Denver at 7:55 p.m. Fare is about $301. The Silversmith Hotel, roughly a five-minute walk from the Palmer House, is about $741 total. Combined estimate: $1,042. Option C: American nonstop at 1:00 p.m., arriving O'Hare at 4:18 p.m.; return at 7:20 p.m., arriving Denver at 9:05 p.m. Fare is about $276. Club Quarters Central Loop, around a ten-minute walk away, is about $648 total. Combined estimate: $924. Option C is the least expensive, but its Thursday arrival leaves the smallest margin.
Take C out. Landing at 4:18 at O'Hare for a 6:30 briefing is tighter than I want. How dependable is A's timing from Midway, and is the Palmer House rate cancellable?

A has the strongest Thursday timing of the three. A 3:25 arrival at Midway leaves about three hours and five minutes before the briefing. Allowing 20 to 30 minutes to get out of the airport and roughly 30 to 50 minutes to reach the hotel still leaves useful slack. The $864 Palmer House total is the flexible rate shown in this comparison, with cancellation permitted until 6:00 p.m. local time two days before arrival. A lower prepaid rate may exist, but it would change the cancellation terms.

That is useful. I would rather not pay the Palmer House premium without seeing whether another nearby hotel gives me essentially the same schedule. Can the Midway flight in A be paired with the Silversmith?

Yes. Pairing A's Southwest flights with the Silversmith gives a fourth combination: the same 12:05 p.m. Denver departure, 3:25 p.m. Midway arrival, and 6:35 p.m. Sunday return, plus three nights at the Silversmith. The estimated total is $1,069: $328 for the flight and $741 for the room. The hotel is on South Wabash, about 0.2 miles from the Palmer House, so the walk is approximately four to six minutes. Compared with staying at the conference hotel, it saves about $123 while preserving the best flight schedule.
Now compare that directly with B. I am mainly trying to understand whether B saves enough to justify O'Hare and the earlier Sunday flight.

B is only about $27 less overall: approximately $1,042 versus $1,069. On Thursday, B lands at O'Hare at 3:45 p.m., 20 minutes later than the Midway itinerary, and the trip downtown is commonly longer and more variable. On Sunday, B leaves at 6:10 p.m., which gives you 35 fewer minutes after the final session. The hotel is identical in both combinations. For a $27 difference, the Midway combination provides materially better timing on both ends.

Agreed. Before we narrow it to that one, is there another hotel within about a ten-minute walk that falls between Club Quarters and the Silversmith in price? It does not need to be attached to the meeting.

The Central Loop Hotel is the clearest middle option in this search. It is about 0.5 miles from the Palmer House, generally an eight-to-ten-minute walk, and the flexible standard-room total is approximately $687 for the three nights. Paired with the Southwest Midway flights, the combined estimate is $1,015. That is $54 less than the Silversmith pairing and $177 less than the Palmer House pairing. The tradeoff is simply the longer walk; the flight schedule remains unchanged.
Please put those three Midway combinations in a compact comparison, including Thursday margin, Sunday timing, walking distance, and total. I want to be sure we are comparing the same rate type.

All three use the same Southwest economy itinerary and flexible hotel rates for March 27 through March 30. Palmer House: flight $328, hotel $864, combined $1,192; conference is in the hotel; Thursday landing at 3:25 p.m. gives 3 hours 5 minutes before the 6:30 briefing; Sunday flight departs at 6:35 p.m., 4 hours 5 minutes after the session ends. Silversmith: flight $328, hotel $741, combined $1,069; approximately a four-to-six-minute walk; the same Thursday and Sunday margins. Central Loop Hotel: flight $328, hotel $687, combined $1,015; approximately an eight-to-ten-minute walk; again the same margins. The hotel totals shown are flexible rather than prepaid, though the exact cancellation deadline should be rechecked on the final booking screen.
The Central Loop combination seems like the best balance. Does the Thursday Southwest fare include a connection, and what is the latest I should plan to be at Denver airport?

It is nonstop. The flight leaves Denver at 12:05 p.m. For a domestic departure, arriving at the terminal around 10:35 a.m. would provide a 90-minute airport window, but that conflicts with your statement that you cannot leave for the airport before 10:30. If you are leaving an office away from the terminal at 10:30, this flight may not be practical unless the trip to DEN is very short. What part of Denver is the morning commitment in, and does it end at 10:30 or can you physically depart at 10:30?

It is downtown and ends at 10:15. I should be able to leave by 10:25, but getting to the airport and through security for a 12:05 departure still sounds uncomfortable. Please check the next nonstop that keeps a reasonable briefing margin.

The next workable nonstop is a 12:55 p.m. departure from Denver, arriving Midway at 4:15 p.m. It is about $22 more round trip when paired with the same 6:35 p.m. Sunday return. Leaving downtown around 10:25 should usually allow you to reach DEN near 11:05, giving roughly one hour and fifty minutes before departure. After the 4:15 Midway arrival, you would have two hours and fifteen minutes before the briefing. A reasonable planning estimate puts you at the Central Loop Hotel around 5:10 to 5:30, leaving time to check in and walk to the Palmer House.
Use that later outbound in the leading combination. I am not asking you to book yet. Give me the final working plan and flag anything I still need to verify.

The leading plan is Southwest nonstop from Denver at 12:55 p.m. Thursday, March 27, arriving Midway at 4:15 p.m.; return nonstop Sunday, March 30 at 6:35 p.m., arriving Denver around 8:15 p.m. Pair it with a standard flexible room at the Central Loop Hotel for three nights. The revised estimate is about $1,037 total: roughly $350 for the flights and $687 for the hotel. The hotel is about an eight-to-ten-minute walk from the Palmer House. This schedule allows about one hour and fifty minutes at DEN if you leave downtown at 10:25, two hours and fifteen minutes between the scheduled Chicago arrival and the exhibitor briefing, and four hours and five minutes between the final session and the return departure. Before booking, verify the live fare, baggage terms, exact hotel taxes, cancellation deadline, and that the Thursday flight remains nonstop. Also confirm the briefing room so you can judge the walk from the hotel accurately.

updated_continuity_summary: Elena Ruiz is planning a solo professional trip from Denver to a university-press rights conference at the Palmer House in Chicago, March 27-30. The working plan is a Thursday 12:55 p.m. nonstop to Midway, a Sunday 6:35 p.m. nonstop return, and three nights at the Central Loop Hotel, estimated at $1,037 combined. The trip has not been booked. Live fare, nonstop status, baggage terms, hotel taxes, cancellation deadline, and briefing-room location remain to be verified.
